summary: Gold edged toward $4,400 an ounce as traders weighed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path after the economy’s main engine showed signs of cooling.

title: Berkshire Boosts Delta, Alphabet Stakes as Abel Taps Cash Pile
summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. padded its holdings in Delta Air Lines Inc. and Google parent Alphabet Inc. during the second quarter as Greg Abel began tapping into the company’s massive cash hoard.

title: Gen Z Moves Money From Stocks to Sports Bets
summary:
Bloomberg's Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Sports betting is increasingly competing with traditional investing for younger Americans’ attention, with more than a quarter of Gen Z investors saying they see gambling on sports as part of their long-term financial strategy, according to a survey by personal finance platform Betterment.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Halved Short Bets on Yen Since Joint Intervention
summary: Hedge funds further dialed back on their wagers against the yen, signaling a reduction in negative sentiment surrounding the currency after the US and Japan’s historic joint intervention.

title: Leveraged ETFs Snap Back as Casino Crowd Mints $50 Billion

title: 'Field of Dreams,' 'Bronx is Burning': Must-Read Baseball Books

Kinsella and "Ladies and Gentlemen, the Bronx Is Burning: 1977, Baseball, Politics, and the Battle for the Soul of a City" by Jonathan Mahler.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Family-Tied Dronemakers (UMAC, PUSA) Get a Boost From New US Tariffs
summary: Drone makers and suppliers, including two companies with ties to the Trump family, rallied Friday after the White House said it’s applying a tariff on imports of unmanned aircraft systems and their components.

title: Dollar Touches Lowest Since May as Retail Data Dims Fed Bets

title: Life Expectancy Must Be Factored in Retirement: Bitterly

title: Oil Producers, Buyers Looking at Long-Term Alternatives to Hormuz, Says Clara Gillispie
summary: Clara Gillispie, senior fellow for climate and energy  at the Council on Foreign Relations, said that both oil producers and buyers are now considering the possibility that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed or operating at a reduced capacity a year in the future. Gillispie said that as countries look for workarounds to the Strait, they are looking both alternative routes and ways to decrease their insurance risk exposure.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: First-Time Homebuyers Find American Dream in Midwest
summary: Bloomberg's Paulina Cachero joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The American Dream of owning a home is alive, at least in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Almost half of all new homeowners in Kent County are younger than 35, as the area is a high concentration of affordable homes and plentiful job opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Codelco Overhauls Management Team as New CEO Seeks Turnaround
summary: Codelco is overhauling management and splitting oversight of its operations into northern and central-southern units as new Chief Executive Officer Jorge Gómez seeks to stabilize mines and finances at one of the world’s largest copper producers.

title: White House Announces Drone Tariffs to Counter China
summary: The Trump Administration announced tariffs on drone imports, seeking to bolster US security and boost domestic defense manufacturing. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall has the details on the new levies and the White House's broader aims to ensure drone dominance. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Rise as Weak Retail Sales Dampen Fed Rate-Hike Expectations
summary: The US two-year yield fell for a third straight week after soft July retail sales data further eroded expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes in the coming months.
